name: Promatic
description: Permit automation for residential plumbing & HVAC contractors — file/manage permits and inspections so jobs aren't stuck waiting on paperwork. ~$99 per project.

mentions.evidence: ~$6.9k L30, ~$15.7k all-time, MRR listed as none (project billing at $99/job), founded May 2025, US. Last sync Oct 1, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: One trade × one bureaucracy (HVAC permits, electrical inspections, dumpster permits) with per-job pricing is an indie-sized wedge.

whyItPrints: Same lane as Easy Moving Permits (Sep 30): contractors hate city portals. Project-priced compliance glue; early but real Stripe L30.
whyThisMatters:
HVAC and plumbing contractors use Promatic so a job doesn't stall in a city permit portal. It files permits, lines up inspections, and keeps licenses and compliance moving. No subscription, and no lock-in. You pay a flat fee per project.

You send the details. They build the package, submit it, and chase the city until it's approved. The permit comes back into your job system. For the inspection they work with you and the homeowner, book the inspector, and stay on it until the permit is closed. Each job has a status, a thread, and someone who owns it.

They work with HVAC crews from Massachusetts to California. Plumbing is the same offer. They put average issuance at five days. A Boston HVAC contractor says those follow-ups keep installations from being delayed. Your office can live in the portals, or Promatic can file and chase the city. The company started in the US in May 2025. You pay when there's a project, so there isn't a monthly seat. There's no contract to sign first.
